hazards.electric-means-no-power: You said electric trucks are too weak for containers. Electric motors are strong, and battery and hydrogen machines are built for this work. The difference is that they make no exhaust where they run.
hazards.exhaust-only-smells: You said exhaust is only a bad smell. Diesel exhaust carries tiny particles that people breathe in. Less exhaust near homes and schools means cleaner air for the neighbours.
hazards.touch-the-charger: You reached for the charging cable. Chargers carry a lot of electricity and only trained crew connect them. Look at the charger from behind the line, and let the crew show how it works.
hazards.walk-into-the-yard: You started into the container yard. Big machines move there all the time, and electric ones are very quiet. Visitors stay behind the yellow line with the crew lead and watch from the walkway.

interrupts.alert: An electric yard tractor rolls past the walkway almost without a sound.
interrupts.cue: Stop, look both ways and wait for the crew lead's signal.
interrupts.missNote: The class kept walking without looking, and the crew lead had to stop everyone at the crossing.
interrupts.why: Electric machines are quiet, so you cannot rely on hearing them. Stopping and looking both ways is the habit that keeps everyone safe. Crews at electric terminals practise the same thing every shift.
interrupts.wrongNote: That relies on hearing the machine. Stop and look both ways. Choose the response that deals with it now.

interrupts.alert: The crew lead asks who helps workers learn the new equipment.
interrupts.cue: Say the Port of Oakland names the Pacific Maritime Association for skills and safety training.
interrupts.missNote: You could not say who helps train the crews, and the crew lead had to explain before the class could go on.
interrupts.why: The Port of Oakland says it partners with the Pacific Maritime Association for skills and safety training on the zero-emission equipment. New machines need crews who know them well. Training is part of every change at a port.
interrupts.wrongNote: That does not name the group the Port says trains the crews. Choose the response that deals with it now.

lateNotes.esa-checkin: The check-in comes at the very end of the visit.
lateNotes.esa-plan-log: The port plan record is written after both filter runs — nothing to record yet.

name: Clean Air at the Port

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Mark the three kinds of machines that move containers around the port.

decoyNotes.esa-gull: Always around the port, but it moves no containers.

itemNotes.esa-crane: It lifts boxes off the ship.
itemNotes.esa-dray: It carries boxes out of the port.
itemNotes.esa-tractor: It moves boxes around the terminal.

steps.prompt: Mark the three kinds of machines that move containers around the port.
steps.title: Find the machines that move containers
steps.why: A port moves containers with several kinds of machines. Cranes lift them off ships, yard tractors pull them around the terminal, and drayage trucks carry them out to warehouses. When these machines run on diesel, they make exhaust right where people work and nearby families live, which is why the kind of power matters.

steps.cue: Clean the filter, run the diesel model, check it, then run the electric model with a clean filter.

itemNames.esa-ord-check: 3 · check the filter for dark specks
itemNames.esa-ord-clean: 1 · fit a clean filter on the exhaust tube
itemNames.esa-ord-electric: 4 · fit a fresh filter and run the electric model

steps.outOfOrderNote: Out of order. Start with a clean filter on the exhaust tube.
steps.prompt: Clean the filter, run the diesel model, check it, then run the electric model with a clean filter.
steps.title: Put the exhaust test in order
steps.why: A fair comparison starts with a clean filter each time. Running the diesel model and checking the filter shows what its exhaust leaves behind. Then a fresh filter and the electric model for the same time shows the difference, with the kind of power as the only change.

steps.cue: Stand behind the yellow line on the walkway with the crew lead.
steps.prompt: Stand behind the yellow line on the walkway with the crew lead.
steps.title: Stay behind the yellow line
steps.why: Container yards are busy places with big machines, and electric machines are so quiet you may not hear them coming. Standing behind the yellow line keeps the class clear of every moving machine. The crew lead watches the yard so the class can watch the lesson.

steps.cue: Turn the timer dial to the teacher's setting for both runs.
steps.prompt: Turn the timer dial to the teacher's setting for both runs.
steps.title: Set the run timer and leave it
steps.why: Both models must run for the same time, or the comparison is not fair. A longer run would leave more specks on the filter no matter what. Setting the timer once for both runs keeps the time the same, so only the kind of power changes.

steps.cue: Commit when the marker matches the filter's colour on the grey scale.

gauge.label: SPECKS
gauge.missNote: Not matched yet. Slide the marker to the grey that looks like the filter.

steps.prompt: Commit when the marker matches the filter's colour on the grey scale.
steps.title: Read the specks on the filter
steps.why: Matching the filter against a grey scale turns what you see into a reading you can compare. A dark filter means more tiny particles, and a clean one means fewer. Scientists who watch air near ports use instruments that do the same job much more precisely.

steps.cue: Hold the filter tube over the model's exhaust until the timer ends.
steps.holdBreakNote: The tube slipped off the exhaust. Hold it steady again until the timer ends.
steps.prompt: Hold the filter tube over the model's exhaust until the timer ends.
steps.title: Hold the filter tube steady
steps.why: If the tube slips, some exhaust escapes past the filter and the reading is too low. Holding it steady catches everything the model gives off. Careful collecting is what makes a comparison honest, for a class model and for real air monitoring.

steps.cue: Drag the model yard tractor to the charging bay on the model yard.

drag.missNote: Not in the charging bay yet. Park it in the marked bay.

steps.prompt: Drag the model yard tractor to the charging bay on the model yard.
steps.title: Park the electric tractor at the charger
steps.why: Electric machines recharge between jobs in a charging yard. Parking in the marked bay puts the machine where trained crew can connect it safely. Planning where machines charge is a big part of switching a port to electric equipment.

steps.cue: Look across the terminal and mark each part of the clean equipment.

decoyNotes.esa-flag: It shows the wind, but it is not equipment.

itemNotes.esa-ev-truck: It carries boxes with no exhaust.

steps.prompt: Look across the terminal and mark each part of the clean equipment.
steps.title: Spot the port's zero-emission equipment
steps.why: The Port of Oakland says its Clean Ports award pays for electric and hydrogen cargo handling equipment, drayage trucks, charging infrastructure and a battery energy storage system. Seeing each kind in the scene helps you picture what a zero-emission port looks like. A battery energy storage system is a set of large batteries that hold electricity until it is needed.

steps.cue: Choose the sentence that says what the two runs showed.
steps.prompt: Choose the sentence that says what the two runs showed.
steps.title: Say what your filters showed
steps.why: Both models ran for the same time with clean filters. The diesel filter came out darker, and the electric filter stayed clean. A good answer says electric machines make no exhaust where they run, and it does not claim more than the two filters showed.

steps.cue: Keep the marker on the smoke puff as the breeze carries it inland.
steps.holdBreakNote: The marker lost the puff. Find it again and follow it with the breeze.
steps.prompt: Keep the marker on the smoke puff as the breeze carries it inland.
steps.title: Follow the breeze from the port
steps.why: Exhaust does not stay where it is made. The breeze carries it over fences and streets to homes and schools. Following the puff shows why cleaner machines at the port help people who live nearby, not only the people who work there.

steps.cue: Write what the Port of Oakland says the award is for and what it expects.
steps.prompt: Write what the Port of Oakland says the award is for and what it expects.
steps.title: Record the port's plan in your own words
steps.why: The Port of Oakland says the Clean Ports Program awarded it three hundred twenty-two million dollars for six hundred sixty-three pieces of zero-emission equipment, and expects a cut of twenty-four thousand tons of greenhouse gas a year and a significant decrease in particulate matter. Writing it in your own words, with the source named, is how a careful reporter works.

steps.cue: Tell another group one reason cleaner air near a port helps people.
steps.prompt: Tell another group one reason cleaner air near a port helps people.
steps.title: Share one reason clean air matters
steps.why: Families, students and workers all breathe the air near a port. Sharing reasons helps the class see how one change at the port reaches many people. Neighbours who live near ports often ask for cleaner air for the same reasons.

steps.cue: Why do electric trucks and cranes help the air? Who breathes that air?
steps.prompt: Why do electric trucks and cranes help the air? Who breathes that air?
steps.title: Check in before leaving the walkway
steps.why: The crew talks over each visit before the class leaves the walkway. Each learner says why electric machines help the air and names who breathes it. If anyone thinks exhaust is only a smell, the group sorts it out now.

tagline: Electric trucks and cranes make no exhaust where they work — see why that matters to the air people breathe
